longForm.overview:
🪭 is the emoji of silk-shade-coded charm — a folding hand fan, the iconography of courtly-pose-coded nostalgia, fold-paper-coded flex, and the universal cool-breeze tag. 🪭 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate silk-shade-coded warmth — a 'fold-paper-coded 🪭' courtly-pose-coded flex or a 'silk-shade-coded 🪭' fold-paper-coded reveal. The fan cue borrows from the universal hand-fan tradition and the modern courtly-pose aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as cool-breeze rather than literal summer item.

In real-world usage 🪭 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate silk-shade-coded warmth. A friend sends it on a 'fold-paper-coded 🪭' courtly-pose-coded reveal. A partner sends it on a 'silk-shade-coded 🪭' fold-paper-coded check-in. A coworker sends it on a 'fold-paper-coded flex 🪭' silk-shade-coded flex. The fan cue is what makes the emoji feel silk-shade-coded — it is not just 'hand fan,' it is 'fold-paper-coded silk-shade flex.'

What separates 🪭 from related object emojis is the courtly-pose register. The emoji is not saying the literal everyday tool, the obvious variant, or the related alt. It is saying 'silk-shade-coded charm,' which carries a specific hand-fan tradition. That is why 🪭 travels especially well on fold-paper-coded flexes, courtly-pose-coded reveals, silk-shade-coded jokes, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with courtly-pose energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:

Avoid 🪭 in work or formal-coded contexts where the silk-shade-coded rule feels off. A 'silk-shade-coded 🪭' Slack message works for a courtly-pose moment; for a more measured update use a sentence or calmer emoji.

Skip 🪭 when you want to communicate soft or bold affection outside the courtly-pose register. The silk-shade-coded tone is too coded for tender or loud moments; use a heart emoji or a sentence when the affection needs to read clearer.
